program.name: Martial Law
program.effect: Morale +10 now, held at 50 or more. Research -20%, ground defense +25%. 10 turns.
program.blocker: Morale is 70: the colony is not in unrest

choices.name: Nebula — Strike Cruiser
choices.description: A Nebula-class hull fitted with a large torpedo pod. Deadliest early in a fight, and well suited to softening up a planet before an invasion.

choices.name: Nebula — Strike Cruiser II
choices.description: Extra launchers and improved torpedo guidance let this Nebula saturate a target before the enemy closes.

choices.name: Edward — Colony Ship
choices.description: Federation colony transport carrying settlers and everything a new human world needs. Unarmed; escort it through contested space.

choices.name: Edward — Colony Ship II
choices.description: A modernized Edward with stronger shields and up-to-date terraforming equipment.

choices.name: Galaxy — Command Cruiser
choices.description: Starfleet's great multi-mission ship, at home on a survey or in a fleet action. Its command facilities coordinate every ship in its task force.

choices.name: Galaxy — Command Cruiser II
choices.description: A service-life refit of the Galaxy class: more weapons, stronger shields and the same superb command suite.

choices.name: Sovereign — Dreadnought
choices.description: The newest ship of the line from Utopia Planitia, pairing long phaser strips and quantum launchers with formidable shields. It also leads the fleet around it.

choices.name: Sovereign — Dreadnought II
choices.description: The Sovereign refit, Starfleet's most heavily armed and best-shielded ship. The last word in Federation design.

choices.name: Miranda — Destroyer
choices.description: An old but trusted Starfleet escort, cheap to build and dependable on frontier patrol against raiders.

choices.name: Miranda — Destroyer II
choices.description: Bigger engines and upgraded arrays turn the Miranda into a quick-reaction escort.

choices.name: Constellation — Heavy Destroyer
choices.description: A four-nacelle escort that is heavier and faster than it looks. Raiders expecting an easy kill regret it.

choices.name: Constellation — Heavy Destroyer II
choices.description: A new drive and shield-penetrating weapon refinements keep this veteran design competitive.

choices.name: Defiant — Heavy Escort
choices.description: A compact, overpowered warship built for one purpose: combat. Fast, heavily armed and able to beat ships twice its size.

choices.name: Oberth — Science Vessel
choices.description: A small Starfleet research ship with long range and excellent sensors. Use it to explore; keep it away from fights.

choices.name: Oberth — Science Vessel II
choices.description: A tougher Oberth with longer sensor reach and enough weapons to survive a bad first contact.

choices.name: London — Troop Transport
choices.description: Starfleet troop and construction transport, used to invade worlds and to build outposts. Unarmed and dependent on escorts.

choices.name: London — Troop Transport II
choices.description: More capacity and heavier shields, so more troops or builders arrive intact.

choices.name: Galaxy-X — Heavy Cruiser
choices.description: A dedicated battleship spun off from the Galaxy design, with a third nacelle and a hull crammed with weapons. It can soak up damage that would gut a lighter ship.

choices.name: Galaxy-X — Heavy Cruiser II
choices.description: The refit tri-nacelle battleship adds heavier guns while keeping pace with escorts.

choices.name: Ambassador — Light Cruiser
choices.description: A sturdy, well-armed Starfleet cruiser for long patrols in dangerous space. Often the first real warship a growing Federation fields.

choices.name: Ambassador — Light Cruiser II
choices.description: The Ambassador refit mounts modern arrays and shields, a clear warning to aggressive neighbors.

choices.name: NX — Light Cruiser
choices.description: Earth's first true deep-space explorer, a warp-five pioneer with polarized hull plating in place of shields. Cheap, reliable and utterly outclassed by anything built a century later.

choices.name: Daedalus — Cruiser
choices.description: A spherical-hulled cruiser from the Federation's founding decades. Roomy and robust, it carried the flag to many first contacts and still makes a stout frontier patrol ship.

roster.source: Model in DS9 (Sisko's office); named in TNG

choices.name: Y-class — Transport
choices.description: A slow boomer freighter whose crews spend their whole lives aboard. It hauls troops and prefabricated structures without complaint, and without much protection.

choices.name: Constitution — Heavy Cruiser
choices.description: The legendary five-year-mission starship: explorer, diplomat and warship in one saucer-and-nacelle silhouette. An early-game workhorse that can do a little of everything.

choices.name: Constitution (refit) — Heavy Cruiser
choices.description: A near-total rebuild of the classic hull with new engines, stronger shields and a denser phaser fit. It stays useful well into the age of the Excelsior.

roster.source: Star Trek: The Motion Picture; films II-VI

choices.name: Soyuz — Frigate
choices.description: A Miranda derivative with an extra sensor and weapons pod bolted aft. Slower than its parent but a far better picket for a border sector.

choices.name: Sydney — Transport
choices.description: A compact personnel transport with a turn of speed its bulk freighter cousins lack. Troops arrive sooner; they do not arrive any safer.

choices.name: Excelsior — Heavy Cruiser
choices.description: Once the great transwarp experiment, later the most numerous capital hull in Starfleet. Tough, long-legged and easy to refit, it anchors many a second-line squadron.

roster.source: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock; TNG, DS9, VOY

choices.name: Raven — Scout
choices.description: A small civilian research ship with an outsized sensor suite. Fragile and unarmed in all but name, it sees far and should never be seen.

choices.name: Challenger — Cruiser
choices.description: A Galaxy-derived cruiser that trades the great saucer for a lean secondary hull. A capable line ship that shares spare parts with half the fleet.

choices.name: Cheyenne — Cruiser
choices.description: A four-nacelle cruiser built around a compact saucer. Its extra warp coils buy acceleration rather than top speed, which suits fleet screening duties.

choices.name: Springfield — Light Cruiser
choices.description: A modular light cruiser whose mission pod swaps between labs, cargo and weapons. Jack of all trades, prized by frontier governors.

choices.name: Freedom — Frigate
choices.description: A single-nacelle frigate that is little more than a saucer with an engine. Fast and cheap; it dies fast and cheap too.

choices.name: Niagara — Heavy Cruiser
choices.description: A three-nacelle heavy cruiser that borrows Galaxy-era components. Solid shields and a deep phaser grid make it a steady anchor for a battle line.

choices.name: New Orleans — Frigate
choices.description: A frigate with twin weapons pods above and below the saucer. It punches above its size and is often assigned to convoy duty.

roster.source: TNG (USS Kyushu, 'The Best of Both Worlds II')

choices.name: Olympic — Science Vessel
choices.description: A spherical-hulled medical and research ship. Its labs and sickbays make it a fine explorer; its weapons are an afterthought.

choices.name: Centaur — Destroyer
choices.description: A compact escort built on Excelsior-era parts with a modern weapons pod. Quick to build and quick in a fight, it filled the gaps of a wartime fleet.

choices.name: Danube — Scout
choices.description: A warp-capable runabout with a swappable mission module. Short range, but cheap, sturdy and far better armed than a shuttle has any right to be.

choices.name: Nova — Science Vessel
choices.description: A small planetary survey ship packed with sensors. Its crew is tiny and its reach is long; it maps a sector in the time a cruiser crosses it.

choices.name: Intrepid — Light Cruiser
choices.description: A fast, variable-geometry explorer with bio-neural computers and the legs for very long missions. Lightly armored but hard to catch, it scouts and skirmishes with equal ease.

choices.name: Yeager — Escort
choices.description: A wartime escort pairing an Intrepid-style saucer with a secondary hull. It was built quickly, in quantity, and it shows.

choices.name: Curry — Frigate
choices.description: An Excelsior reworked into a gunship by trading its saucer lab space for weapons. Ugly, effective and cheap to field from older hulls.

choices.name: Akira — Strike Cruiser
choices.description: A heavy torpedo cruiser with a launcher pod slung between twin hulls. It opens battles with a salvo few shields survive, then relies on escorts while it reloads.

choices.name: Steamrunner — Destroyer
choices.description: A flat, broad-winged destroyer that presents a small target head-on. Designed for the Borg threat and pressed into service everywhere after.

choices.name: Saber — Escort
choices.description: A small, agile escort that fills the space between runabout and frigate. Cheap enough to lose, quick enough to outrun what it cannot kill.

choices.name: Norway — Light Cruiser
choices.description: A compact cruiser tuned for rapid response. It shares a design philosophy with the Akira but trades the torpedo pod for longer endurance.

choices.name: Prometheus — Battlecruiser
choices.description: An experimental tactical cruiser that splits into three independent attack vectors. Few designs can match its alpha strike, and none match its price tag.

choices.name: Rhode Island — Frigate
choices.description: A Nova hull rebuilt as a fighting frigate. It keeps the survey pedigree but gains the teeth to defend the systems it charts.

choices.name: Peregrine — Raider
choices.description: A fast courier ship used for dispatches in peacetime and for hit-and-run raids by anyone who can get one. Fragile but very quick.
